- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days — cap forecast decline to 5–7% below peak.
- If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust quickly — apply lagged sentiment smoothing to forecast curve.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently 2–3% above true price for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early decline after volatility — reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–2% relative to historical 18-day mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.9 → -0.6 → +0.8), model underreacts — add 0.3–0.5% buffer to forecast during sentiment shift windows.
